verdict.rationale: GitCafe documents Git over SSH and states that accounts created via GitHub sync receive the SSH keys from the user's GitHub profile with default SSH access, so SSH keys are an account-level credential for Git. However, the evidence never shows a user adding or managing their own SSH keys directly in GitCafe. missing for 10: documented manual SSH key registration and management (add/remove keys in settings or via CLI/API), key access scopes, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can register SSH keys on my account to authenticate Git operations

citations.quote: GitCafe repositories work with any Git client over HTTPS or SSH.
Your new account also gets the SSH and GPG keys on your GitHub profile, with the default SSH access; keys GitCafe cannot use are skipped.
